newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori denies he may free jailed rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori denies he may free jailed rebels.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori on Thursday vehemently denied that his government would free jailed Marxist rebels in a deal to end the 93-day-old hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's Lima home.

"My government's position remains the same. There will be no freeing of MRTA prisoners," Fujimori said in a radio interview from the central Andes, referring to jailed members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement.

Fujimori was responding to media speculation that he may have agreed after meeting Japan's Vice Foreign Minister Masahiko Komura this week to free some MRTA prisoners to secure the release of 72 hostages held by 20-odd MRTA rebels.
Fujimori has denied the main rebel demand since the MRTA stormed the Japanese residence Dec. 17.
"I absolutely, totally and flatly deny the positon of my government has changed," Fujimori told Radioprogramas del Peru on Thursday. "The security of the country comes before any other interest."

Fujimori said his government would continue searching for a peaceful end to the crisis and Tuesday's discussions with Komura had served better to coordinate efforts to find asylum for the rebels in another country.
